title: AI Rules Manager
summary: Makes every change to the Fusion AI Rules repository: adds, changes, deprecates or accepts rules, bumps the version, builds, opens a pull request, and republishes the Rule Set page.
what_it_is: A Claude skill for maintaining Swami's **Fusion AI Rules**: good-practice rules for AIs that model in Autodesk Fusion. The public GitHub repository `swami-claude-skills/fusion-ai-rules` is the single source of truth, with one YAML file per rule.

Swami asks for a change in plain words. Claude edits the files on a branch, runs the build checks, picks the version bump, updates the change log and page text, and opens a pull request. Swami approves the merge, and GitHub then builds the exports, the GitHub Pages site and the release by itself.
why: The rules are used by several AIs and by other people. Keeping them in one repository with a fixed process means every change is reviewed, versioned and exported the same way, and nobody has to remember the steps.

what_it_does.text: Adds a new rule as `rules/R##-slug.yaml`, or changes one, in the existing field order. Rule IDs are permanent and never reused.
Bumps `ruleset.yaml`: patch for a wording fix, minor for a new rule or export target, major for a rule removed or deprecated, a meaning changed, or a priority raised to Must.
Never deletes a rule: marks it Deprecated and points to the replacement, which lists it under `supersedes`.
Clears `conflicts_with` between active rules, since the build check fails while two active rules name each other.
Promotes accepted candidates from `candidates/` to `rules/` under their proposed IDs, records the decisions in `sources/`, and checks the author has agreed to CC BY 4.0.
Runs `python3 build/build.py check` and `build`, and reports any export target that falls back to a smaller selection or titles only.
Adds a test question for each new rule in `tests/prompts/`, turns results from the Test result form into `tests/results/` files, and changes a rule's status only when the results back it.
Updates the Rule Set page text and its spoken overview when the rule count or meaning changes, re-recording with the vibe-dashboard skill.
Scans for private details, pushes a branch, opens a pull request through the GitHub REST API with the repository's template, and watches it.
After the merge, checks the Action and Pages deploy, then rebuilds Swami's Claude copy of the Rule Set page with its private links and republishes it.
Refreshes Swami's private Rules Admin page after rules or results change.

flow.heading: AI RULES MANAGER · ONE CHANGE, START TO FINISH
flow.tip: How one change moves from a branch through the build check, privacy scan and pull request to Swami's merge, the GitHub Action and the republished pages, with proposals and test results feeding in.
flow.alt: Workflow diagram: proposals from the issue form become candidate files reviewed with ai-rule-review, and test results become results files. A change goes 1 branch from main, 2 edit the rule YAML, 3 bump the version and add a changelog entry and tests, 4 run the build check, 5 privacy scan and open a pull request, 6 Swami merges, 7 the GitHub Action builds, deploys Pages and creates a release, 8 Claude republishes the Rule Set page and refreshes the Rules Admin page.
flow.caption: Read left to right along the middle row, then right to left along the bottom row. The dashed boxes on top are the two ways outside input arrives. Only step 6 is Swami's; nothing on GitHub can authorize a merge.

how_to_use.step: In the Fusion AI Rules project, say what should change in plain words.
Claude makes a branch, edits the YAML files, bumps the version and updates `CHANGELOG.md`.
Claude runs the build check and build, updates page text and audio if needed, and scans for private details.
Claude opens a pull request and sends the link. Read it on GitHub.
Merge it on GitHub, or tell Claude to merge it; Claude merges only when you ask. Branch protection requires the `check` to pass first.
The GitHub Action builds the exports, deploys Pages and makes a release if the version is new. Claude checks it and republishes the Claude copy of the Rule Set page.

how_to_use_windows.step: Nothing runs on your computer, so the steps are the same on Windows 10 or 11: ask in the project, review the pull request on GitHub in Edge or Chrome, and merge.

capabilities.text: Every change goes through a branch, a passing build check and a pull request, so main never breaks.
Picks the version bump from the kind of change, so a release number tells readers how big the change is.
Exports for all AIs, the public site and the release are rebuilt automatically from the merged files.

limitations.text: Claude never merges without Swami's own go-ahead; a GitHub comment can't authorize it.
GitHub's GraphQL API, Pages settings and branch protection settings are blocked from Claude sessions, so it uses the REST API and Swami changes settings himself.
The github.io site can't be opened from Claude's workspace; deploys are checked through the GitHub deployments API instead.

scheduled_tasks.summary: None. It runs when Swami asks for a rule change or a review. The repository's GitHub Action builds and publishes on every merge, but that is GitHub, not a Claude scheduled task.

other_ais.notes: Skills need a Business, Enterprise, Edu, or Healthcare plan. It would also need write access to the GitHub repo, which ChatGPT doesn't normally have. Swami tests in Claude only.
Upload the unzipped skill folder. Without GitHub write access it can only draft the YAML changes for someone else to commit. Swami tests in Claude only.
Import the .zip (or the SKILL.md if refused). Same GitHub limits as the others. Swami tests in Claude only.

gotchas.text: Deleting a rule file breaks links and history. Deprecate it instead.
`private.json` holds the private links for the Claude copy. It lives only in project files and must never be committed.
Long rules push size-limited export targets down to Must only or titles only. The build allows it, but say so in the pull request.
Never test branch protection by pushing to main; it records a commit that can't be cleanly removed.

requirements.text: Swami's GitHub connected to Claude, with the fusion-ai-rules repository attached with push access.
The Fusion AI Rules Claude project, for `private.json` and project memory.

glossary.def: Swami's set of good-practice rules for AIs that model in Autodesk Fusion, kept in a public GitHub repository.
The dashboard that shows every rule and exports them for each AI. A public copy is on GitHub Pages and a Claude copy has Swami's private links.
The GitHub project that holds every rule file, the build script and the site; the single source of truth.
A proposed set of changes on a branch, reviewed and checked before it is merged into main.
A GitHub setting on main that requires a pull request and a passing check before anything is merged, for everyone.
The automated job that checks every change, and on merge builds the exports, deploys GitHub Pages and makes a release.
GitHub's free web hosting, which serves the public Rule Set page and downloads.
GitHub's web interface for scripts; used because the GraphQL API is blocked from Claude sessions.
A plain-text file format; each rule is one YAML file with fixed fields.
A proposed rule waiting for review, kept in `candidates/` with a proposed ID.
A rule that is retired but kept, pointing to the rule that replaces it.
The rule set's version number: patch for wording, minor for new rules or targets, major for removals or meaning changes.
One place a rule file goes, such as a Claude project or a ChatGPT custom GPT, each with its own format and size limit.
The open licence for the rule text: anyone can reuse it with credit. Authors of new rules agree to it.
The script step that validates every rule, test and setting, and fails on errors such as conflicting active rules.
A GitHub issue form for sending the results of a test kit run in one AI; Claude turns each into a results file.
